newsitem.title: CANADA: FALCONBRIDGE RECEIVES UNION SHIFT PROPOSAL.
newsitem.headline: FALCONBRIDGE RECEIVES UNION SHIFT PROPOSAL.

text.p: The union representing Falconbridge Ltd's striking Ontario workers said on Monday it was awaiting the company's response to a union proposal on shift scheduling.
Union and company negotiators have not met since about 1,400 workers walked off the job on August 1.
Rolly Gauthier, local 598 president of the Canadian Auto Workers union, said a union subcommittee delivered a proposal on shift scheduling to the company on Friday.
"We're waiting for the company to respond to our last position on Friday," Gauthier said in a telephone interview.
"Nothing happened over the weekend and it's too early on Monday morning for anything to happen," he said.
Falconbridge officials were unavailable for comment.
Falconbridge's Sudbury operations last year produced 45,700 metric tons of nickel, 50,000 metric tons of copper and 1,600 metric tons of cobalt, including custom feed.
